subject: That scary pop-up is lying
preheader: A fake virus warning, why updates matter, and a thank-you note in seconds.
intro: Short and useful, as always. Start with the pop-up.

sections.label: Scam of the week
sections.title: The pop-up that says your computer is infected
paragraphs: A loud warning fills your screen with a phone number to call "Microsoft" or "Apple Support." It may even beep. It's a trick.
bullets: Real companies don't put phone numbers in pop-ups.
Don't call, and don't click anything inside the box.
Close the browser tab or app. If it won't close, restart the computer. Never let anyone take remote control of your computer.

sections.label: Tip of the week
sections.title: Keep your phone up to date
paragraphs: Updates fix security holes that scammers use. Make it a habit.
bullets: iPhone: Settings, then General, then Software Update.
Android: open Settings and search for "software update."
If it says you're up to date, you're done. If not, plug the phone in and tap Update, ideally overnight.

sections.label: AI trick of the week
sections.title: Write a thank-you note
paragraphs: Let AI write the first draft, then make it yours.
sections.prompt: Write a warm three-sentence thank-you note to my neighbor Pat for watching my dog last weekend.
sections.note: Change the name and the details, and it's your note.
